questions.q: According to this lesson, what is "the Salesforce Platform"?
options: Another name for Sales Cloud specifically
The underlying database, security model, and customization/development tools everything else is built on
A third-party product unrelated to Salesforce applications
A marketing term with no technical meaning
questions.explain: The platform is the foundation — strip away a named application like Sales Cloud, and the platform underneath is still fully functional.

questions.q: What is a Salesforce "application," as defined in this lesson?
options: The same thing as the platform itself
Any custom object a user creates
A specific, pre-built product — like Sales Cloud or Service Cloud — built on top of the platform
A mobile app only, never a browser-based product
questions.explain: Applications are what's built on the platform for a specific job, such as the named clouds from Lesson 7.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the platform and applications?
options: The platform is a feature inside Sales Cloud, not the other way around
Applications and the platform are entirely unrelated products
Only Service Cloud is built on the Salesforce Platform
Every application ships on the platform, but not everything built on the platform is one of the named CRM applications
questions.explain: This is the core relationship the lesson draws out — applications are built on the platform, but the platform is general-purpose beyond any one application.

questions.q: Which example does this lesson give of something built on the Salesforce Platform that has nothing to do with CRM?
options: A new version of Sales Cloud's lead object
A rebranded copy of Service Cloud
An upgraded AppExchange listing page
An internal app for tracking equipment maintenance
questions.explain: The lesson gives equipment maintenance tracking, event registration portals, and industry-specific custom apps as examples of non-CRM uses of the platform.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect the platform/application distinction to Salesforce careers?
options: Administrators and developers do exactly the same work with no distinction
Only developers are allowed to use the Salesforce Platform at all
An administrator mostly configures existing applications, while a developer builds new custom applications directly on the platform
Administrators build new applications and developers only configure existing ones
questions.explain: The lesson previews Lesson 10's role breakdown: admins mostly customize pre-built applications, while developers build new things on the platform underneath.
